entries.description: Harry recalls the castle’s secret passages and ghosts, Great Hall banquets, a four-poster in the tower dormitory, Hagrid’s cabin next to the Forbidden Forest, and six tall Quidditch goalposts.
entries.model_notes: A narrated recap reaffirming established features; no new floor plan or numeric goalpost height.

entries.description: Hagrid says flesh-eating slugs are ruining the school cabbages and that he is buying repellent.
entries.model_notes: Establishes school cabbage-growing and a pest problem, without identifying a bed, greenhouse or location beside Hagrid’s hut.

entries.description: The usually traversable barrier between platforms nine and ten becomes solid to Harry and Ron after the other Weasleys pass through. Their trolleys collide, pushing does not open it, and no train sound is audible through the cold metal.
entries.model_notes: Remote school-transport access state; its cause is not yet known. The gateway is concealed from Muggle sight.

entries.description: The boys follow the Hogwarts Express north, using the car’s compass and repeated checks. Fields give way to purple moors, villages and a large city; later the railway winds past a snow-capped mountain.
entries.model_notes: North is the observed journey heading, not a castle facade bearing. No city or mountain is named.

entries.location: Castle cliff and lake — aerial view
entries.description: Hogwarts’ many towers and turrets silhouette the horizon on a cliff above the lake. The car approaches over the smooth black water, described as a mile below, with the castle ahead.
entries.model_notes: Mile refers to an aerial separation estimate at that moment, not the height of the supporting cliff.

entries.location: Aerial crash route — castle wall to Willow
entries.description: The descending car almost hits a dark stone castle wall, turns in an arc over dark greenhouses, then a vegetable patch, then black lawns, and hits a thick tree trunk.
entries.model_notes: Explicit ordered overflight; no compass side, spacing or proof that the cabbages occupy this particular patch.

entries.description: The ancient gnarled tree bends its trunk almost double and strikes the car with twisted branches, thick boughs and knucklelike twigs. Its roots creak as it reaches after the reversing car, and its branches continue flailing after escape.
entries.model_notes: The name comes from Snape’s later identification. Reach and trunk size are relative; no numeric safety radius established.

entries.description: Snape reports considerable damage to the old valuable Whomping Willow after the car collision.
entries.model_notes: Reported damage without itemised broken branches; car dents do not establish corresponding tree wounds.

entries.location: Whomping Willow vicinity to front entrance
entries.description: After being ejected onto damp ground, the boys drag trunks up a grassy slope towards the huge oak front doors, leaving luggage at the foot of the front steps.
entries.model_notes: Confirms a lower crash area relative to the entrance approach; no distance from Willow to doors.

entries.location: Great Hall — exterior window sightline and sorting
entries.description: From a brightly lit window near the front steps the boys watch sorting inside the Great Hall: hovering candles above four long tables, golden plates and goblets, the starry ceiling, and a stool for the Sorting Hat before the first-years.
entries.model_notes: Exterior visibility of Hall interior is a significant constraint. No window side, sill height or exact angle is given.

entries.description: Snape takes them up the steps into the vast torchlit echoing Entrance Hall, then down a narrow stone staircase into the dungeons, opening a door halfway along a cold passage to his office.
entries.model_notes: Office door is halfway along this passage; passage length and dungeon level are not specified.

entries.location: Snape’s office — jars, desk and hearth seating
entries.description: Shelves of large specimen jars line the shadowy walls. A large slimy object in green liquid stands on a shelf behind the desk. The initially empty fireplace is lit by McGonagall’s wand, and two chairs stand beside it.
entries.model_notes: Office distinct from Potions classroom; a usable hearth and desk-relative specimen shelf are observed.

entries.description: McGonagall produces sandwiches, two silver goblets and iced pumpkin juice on Snape’s desk; the sandwich plate refills as the boys eat.
entries.model_notes: Temporary office meal service, not a permanent catering installation.

entries.description: The return route passes murmuring portraits and creaking suits of armour, climbs narrow stone stair flights and reaches the passage containing the Fat Lady’s oil painting in a pink silk dress.
entries.model_notes: Adds stair materials, sounds and portrait medium; no complete turn-by-turn map.

entries.location: Gryffindor common room — password and tables
entries.description: The new password Wattlebird opens the portrait onto the crowded circular common room, whose furniture includes lop-sided tables and squashy armchairs.
entries.model_notes: Furniture shapes are observed during a temporary welcome crowd; password dated to this arrival.

entries.description: A door across the common room leads to a spiral stair. Climbing right to its top reaches the same circular dormitory as last year, now signed second-years, with five red-velvet-hung four-posters and high narrow windows. Trunks stand at bed ends.
entries.model_notes: Same cohort retains the room while its sign changes. Right to the top describes this route at this time; tower-storey count remains unspecified.

entries.location: Great Hall — cloudy ceiling and Howler acoustics
entries.description: The ceiling mirrors a dull grey cloudy sky over the four breakfast tables. Ron’s Howler fills the Hall with amplified sound, rattling tableware, echoing from stone walls and shaking dust from the ceiling.
entries.model_notes: Observed acoustic and ceiling behaviour; no sound-pressure level or ceiling construction inferred.

entries.location: Castle, vegetable patch, greenhouses and Willow
entries.description: The pupils leave the castle and cross the vegetable patch to the greenhouses. From outside the greenhouses, the Willow is visible in the distance with several branches in slings; Sprout approaches across the lawn carrying bandages.
entries.model_notes: Adds ground route and sightline; sling damage state dated after the car crash.

entries.location: Greenhouse Three — access and hanging flowers
entries.description: Sprout unlocks Greenhouse Three with a large belt key; pupils have previously worked only in Greenhouse One. Three contains more dangerous plants, damp earth and fertiliser smells, and strongly perfumed umbrella-sized flowers hanging from the ceiling.
entries.model_notes: At least separately numbered One and Three exist; numbering alone does not describe greenhouse Two. Door is lockable.

entries.location: Greenhouse Three — teaching bench and Mandrakes
entries.description: A trestle bench stands centrally with about twenty pairs of coloured earmuffs. Deep trays hold roughly a hundred purple-green seedling Mandrakes in rows; pots are stored under the table, with more pots and sacks of compost available. Four pupils work to each tray.
entries.model_notes: Layout and safety equipment for the repotting lesson; quantities are approximate.

entries.description: The Mandrake earmuffs block all sound; Sprout says seedling cries cause hours of unconsciousness while mature cries are fatal. A spiky dark-red Venomous Tentacula extends long feelers towards her and withdraws after a slap.
entries.model_notes: Sound blocking and Tentacula response are observed; cry hazards are taught by Hermione/Sprout, not tested on pupils.

entries.location: Courtyard — stone step and side-door route
entries.description: After lunch the pupils go into the courtyard, where Hermione sits on a stone step and voices echo. Lockhart takes Harry into the castle through a side door, down a corridor and up a staircase to his classroom.
entries.model_notes: Links courtyard side entrance to an ascending classroom route without a floor number; class bells are audible outside.

entries.location: Defence classroom — furniture and window relation
entries.description: Lockhart’s classroom has pupil desks, his desk at the front, wall pictures, ink bottles, a waste bin, a window by the back rows, and a ceiling candelabrum. He places a large covered cage on his desk.
entries.model_notes: Window proximity inferred directly from the back row showered with glass, not a measured window-wall plan.

entries.description: Released Cornish pixies shatter a window, spray ink, shred papers and books, tear pictures from walls and overturn the bin, throwing objects outside. Neville hangs from the candelabrum, which later gives way, dropping him. Pupils shelter beneath desks; remaining pixies are immobilised and recaged.
entries.model_notes: First-lesson damage state; no repair timing is supplied.

entries.location: Castle to Quidditch stadium — dawn route
entries.description: Harry descends the dormitory spiral stair, crosses the common room, exits the portrait hole and leaves the castle for dew-covered grass and sloping lawns down to the stadium changing rooms.
entries.model_notes: Reaffirms downhill pitch route; dawn mist and birdsong are seasonal scene conditions.

entries.location: Quidditch changing room — seating and tactics boards
entries.description: Players sit on opposite sides of the changing room with a wall behind one side; Wood presents three boards of pitch diagrams, with coloured arrows animated by a wand tap.
entries.model_notes: Seating is observed without a specified bench form. Portable tactical boards do not fix pitch shape beyond the text.

entries.location: Quidditch stadium — high seats and sound
entries.description: Colin occupies one of the highest spectator seats; his camera clicks sound strangely amplified across the otherwise deserted stadium. Players fly round the stadium and a corner.
entries.model_notes: Corner wording alone is insufficient for a rectangular field or square stands.

entries.location: Stadium to Hagrid’s hut — nearby refuge
entries.description: Harry calls Hagrid’s the nearest place to take Ron. They leave the stadium, cross the grounds towards the Forest’s edge, and hide behind a nearby bush within twenty feet of the cabin when Lockhart emerges.
entries.model_notes: Observed route and bush proximity; nearest is Harry’s judgment, not a measured comparison with hospital distance.

entries.location: Hagrid’s cabin — corners, table and basin
entries.description: The one-room cabin has an enormous bed in one corner and a crackling fire in another. Chairs surround a scrubbed table used for tea; Hagrid brings a large copper basin for Ron.
entries.model_notes: Adds separate bed/fire corners and table finish; rooster and basin are temporary objects.

entries.description: A small vegetable patch behind the cabin contains about a dozen boulder-sized pumpkins being grown for the Hallowe’en feast. Hagrid’s pink umbrella leans against the cabin’s back wall.
entries.model_notes: Pumpkins receive admitted magical help; Hermione proposes an Engorgement Charm. This patch is not automatically identical to the castle-to-greenhouse vegetable patch.

entries.description: The pupils walk back uphill to the castle and enter the cool Entrance Hall before proceeding into the Great Hall for lunch.
entries.model_notes: Confirms castle above hut approach; no path material or precise distance.

entries.location: Trophy room — silver and named awards
entries.description: Ron’s detention involves polishing silver trophies without magic. He later reports repeatedly cleaning the Quidditch Cup and a Special Award for Services to the School.
entries.model_notes: Named displayed awards and polishing; Ron’s estimate of a hundred cups is not an exact inventory.

entries.location: Lockhart’s office — second floor and photographs
entries.description: Harry reaches Lockhart’s office along the second-floor corridor. Many candles light countless framed photographs of Lockhart on the walls; another large pile of photographs lies on his desk.
entries.model_notes: Explicit office floor, desk and candlelit self-portrait decor; office is separate from classroom.

entries.description: During detention Harry hears a venomous disembodied voice while Lockhart says he hears nothing. The office otherwise contains candle sounds and Lockhart’s speech.
entries.model_notes: Dated acoustic event, not proof of an invisible occupant or of a door opening; source route unresolved at this point.

entries.location: Grounds and castle — prolonged autumn rain
entries.description: Damp chill enters grounds and castle. Days of heavy rain thunder on the windows, raise the lake, turn flowerbeds into muddy streams and swell Hagrid’s pumpkins to garden-shed size.
entries.model_notes: Flooded planting beds and lake rise are seasonal, with no numeric level change.

entries.description: Nick reports that third-years plastered frog brains over the ceiling in dungeon five and that Filch has been cleaning it.
entries.model_notes: Named/numbered dungeon, not identified as the usual Potions room.

entries.location: Upper corridor tapestry route to Filch’s office
entries.description: Filch emerges through a tapestry on Harry’s right in a corridor with a window, then takes him downstairs to his office. Harry later leaves the office along a corridor and climbs back upstairs.
entries.model_notes: Relative floor change only; tapestry suggests concealed circulation but no passage destination is independently mapped.

entries.description: The office is dingy and windowless, with a low ceiling supporting a single hanging oil lamp and a faint fried-fish smell. Wooden filing cabinets line the walls; a desk with drawers and quill/ink containers faces a wall display of polished chains and manacles. A moth-eaten chair stands beside the desk.
entries.model_notes: Punishment records occupy labelled cabinets, including a drawer for Fred and George. Ceiling-hanging punishments remain a reported request, not current practice.

entries.location: Classroom over Filch’s office — damaged cabinet
entries.description: A loud overhead crash rattles Filch’s lamp. Back upstairs Harry sees the wreckage of a large black-and-gold cabinet in a classroom; Nick says he had Peeves crash it directly above the office, and Filch calls it a valuable vanishing cabinet.
entries.model_notes: Observed wreckage plus reported identity and cause. No paired cabinet, transport destination or later repair inferred.

entries.description: A fire-dwelling orange salamander smoulders on a table among armchairs before the twins’ firework makes it whirl about the common room shedding sparks and orange stars; it escapes into the hearth with explosions.
entries.model_notes: Temporary magical disturbance; no lasting furniture damage is stated.

entries.description: The Hall is decorated with live bats and huge pumpkin lanterns, large enough for three men to sit inside. Golden plates and candles glitter at the packed feast; dancing skeleton entertainment is only rumoured.
entries.model_notes: Pumpkin scale is explicit but not numeric; keep the skeleton troupe unconfirmed.

entries.location: Great Hall approach to Deathday dungeon
entries.description: At seven the trio pass the Great Hall doorway and head down towards the dungeons. The party passage is lined with thin black candles burning blue; temperature drops along it. A corner leads to a doorway draped in black velvet.
entries.model_notes: A roomier dungeon is the reported venue. No dungeon number or relation to Snape’s office is supplied.

entries.location: Deathday dungeon — dance floor, orchestra and chandelier
entries.description: Hundreds of translucent ghosts crowd a dance floor. An orchestra of thirty musical saws performs on a black-draped platform; a chandelier holds a thousand black candles with midnight-blue flames. The dungeon is cold enough to mist the pupils’ breath.
entries.model_notes: Party installation includes a podium in an icy-blue spotlight and wall-penetrating ghost horses. No physical stable or horse-access door is required.

entries.description: Across the dungeon a long black-velvet-covered table holds rotten fish on silver platters, burnt cakes on salvers, maggoty haggis, mouldy cheese and a tombstone-shaped anniversary cake. Ghosts pass through the table and food to try tasting them.
entries.model_notes: Temporary olfactory and table arrangement; ghost permeability does not imply walk-through solid surfaces for people.

entries.location: Myrtle’s girls’ toilet — floor and disrepair report
entries.description: Hermione identifies Myrtle’s haunt as the girls’ toilet on the first floor, out of order all year because Myrtle’s tantrums flood it.
entries.model_notes: Preserve this reported first-floor placement; reconcile separately with subsequent journey descriptions rather than silently changing it.

entries.location: Deathday dungeon to second-floor writing corridor
entries.description: Leaving the dungeon, the trio return up the candlelit passage towards the Entrance Hall steps. Harry follows a voice apparently moving upward, climbs into the Entrance Hall, up the marble staircase to the first floor, then another flight to the second; he runs round that floor to its last deserted passage.
entries.model_notes: Floor sequence explicit. Sound source travelling through ceilings is Harry’s hypothesis; no phantom route is established.

entries.location: Second-floor writing corridor — windows, torches, water and cat
entries.description: Foot-high warning words about the Chamber’s opening shine on a wall between two windows in torchlight. A large puddle covers the nearby floor; Mrs Norris hangs stiffly by her tail from a torch bracket beneath the writing. After the feast, pupils reach this passage from both ends via stairs.
entries.model_notes: Dated attack state with two-ended circulation, windows and bracket; no ink material, window spacing or exact stair count.

entries.description: Lockhart offers his office as nearest and just upstairs from the attack scene. The party enters its darkened interior, where desk candles are lit and the petrified cat is laid on a polished desk while others sit in chairs.
entries.model_notes: Just upstairs conflicts with chapter 7’s second-floor office and chapter 8’s second-floor attack route. Preserve source statements independently.

entries.description: Leaving the office, the trio go one floor up, enter an empty classroom and close the door to confer. A distant clock chimes midnight.
entries.model_notes: Relative office-plus-one floor, with no absolute floor assigned because of office-placement conflict.

entries.location: Attack corridor — resistant writing and guard chair
entries.description: Filch’s magical cleaning fluid fails to remove the shining words from the stone wall. Later the cat is gone and an empty guard chair stands against the message wall.
entries.model_notes: Dated persistent inscription and movable chair. Material of the writing remains unknown.

entries.description: Harry is kept after Potions to scrape tubeworms from the desks.
entries.model_notes: Adds desk cleanup state; no permanent infestation implied.

entries.location: History of Magic classroom and staff-room memory
entries.description: Binns enters his classroom through the blackboard; the room has pupil desks and a window through which Dean looks. His death story places an armchair in front of the staff-room fire.
entries.model_notes: Classroom fixtures directly narrated; death anecdote reports historical armchair/hearth arrangement without date.

entries.description: Binns says the four founders built the castle together more than a thousand years earlier, at an uncertain date, far from Muggle observation during an age of persecution.
entries.model_notes: Historical report of age and seclusion; no foundation plan or location coordinates.

entries.description: Binns recounts the legend that Slytherin secretly built and sealed a chamber in the castle, unknown to the other founders, which only his true heir could unseal to release a controllable monster against supposedly unworthy pupils.
entries.model_notes: A contested legend at this point; not observed chamber geometry or a verified biological access rule.

entries.description: Binns says learned witches and wizards, including successive heads, have searched the school repeatedly without finding a chamber, and denies that it or its monster exists.
entries.model_notes: Reported negative search history and interpretation. Lack of discovery must not erase later positive observations.

entries.location: Attack corridor — scorch marks and spider window
entries.description: Harry finds scorch marks on the corridor floor. At the window next to the writing, about twenty spiders climb a long silvery thread and crowd a small crack in the topmost glass pane, apparently trying to escape outdoors.
entries.model_notes: Physical marks, cracked high pane and external opening; reason for spider flight not yet demonstrated.

entries.description: A few paces beyond Filch’s chair, at the former puddle’s level, a brass-knobbed door marked Out of Order leads into Myrtle’s girls’ toilet. Hermione calls the cat’s attack site immediately outside its front door. Percy later appears at the head of nearby stairs.
entries.model_notes: Observed adjacency ties bathroom to the previously narrated second-floor corridor; conflicts with Hermione’s first-floor report in chapter 8.

entries.description: A large cracked spotted dirty mirror hangs above a row of chipped stone sinks. Damp flooring reflects dim light from low candle stubs in holders. Wooden cubicle doors are scratched and flaking, with one hanging from its hinges.
entries.model_notes: Detailed neglected state; no sink or cubicle count. The end cubicle contains a toilet with a cistern.

entries.location: Myrtle’s bathroom — ghost and toilet water
entries.description: Myrtle floats on the end-cubicle cistern, then dives headfirst into the toilet, splashing the visitors; muffled sobbing comes from the U-bend.
entries.model_notes: Ghost interaction with water and plumbing is observed; no human-accessible tunnel is established here.

entries.description: Borrowing a book from the Restricted Section requires a teacher’s signed permission note.
entries.model_notes: Repeated rule now explicitly concerns checking out a book; not a magical ward description.

entries.description: Pince inspects the teacher’s note against the light, then retrieves the restricted potion book from among lofty shelves. The library is markedly quiet.
entries.model_notes: Observed administrative access, no automatic magical authentication or measured shelf height.

entries.location: Library to Myrtle’s bathroom — private worksite
entries.description: Within five minutes of leaving the library the trio barricade themselves in the out-of-order bathroom. Myrtle occupies her own cubicle; Hermione chooses the room because other pupils avoid it.
entries.model_notes: Five minutes is this narrated transition, not a measured distance or direct adjacency.

entries.location: Potion ingredients — student cupboard and private stores
entries.description: Hermione says common ingredients can be taken from the student store-cupboard. Harry distinguishes rarer materials unavailable there and proposes breaking into Snape’s private stores.
entries.model_notes: Reported separate storage provisions; lock status and locations are not yet observed.

entries.description: Wood says the Bludgers have been kept locked in Madam Hooch’s office since the last practice.
entries.model_notes: Reported office storage and locked access; no office floor or link to the changing room.

entries.location: Quidditch pitch — rain, mud and rogue Bludger
entries.description: Heavy rain reduces visibility during the match and turns the landing surface muddy. One Bludger repeatedly pursues Harry despite being struck away; after the match the twins restrain it in a box.
entries.model_notes: A temporary altered ball behaviour, not a change to the pitch’s normal boundaries or rules.

entries.location: Hospital wing — privacy curtains and bedside supplies
entries.description: A curtain can be drawn around Harry’s bed for changing. A bedside table holds a water jug; bed pillows and supplies for water and medicine are available. Visitors enter through the ward door.
entries.model_notes: Adds curtained bedside privacy and water vessel; no unsupported curtain track geometry.

entries.description: Dobby appears at Harry’s bedside during the dark night and, hearing approaching footsteps, vanishes with a loud crack while Harry is holding his wrist.
entries.model_notes: Observed departure inside Hogwarts. Arrival itself is not witnessed and the mechanism is not named here.

entries.description: Dobby admits hiding at King’s Cross and sealing the gateway to prevent Harry reaching the school train.
entries.model_notes: Resolves the temporary transport obstruction’s cause by character admission; no claim that the normal gateway closes at eleven.

entries.location: Hospital wing — beds, passage and matron access
entries.description: Dumbledore and McGonagall carry Colin in from the outside passage and lay him on a bed three beds from Harry. McGonagall passes Harry’s bed to fetch Pomfrey and returns with her; moonlight illuminates Colin.
entries.model_notes: At least the observed relative bed spacing; do not invent a precise total bed count or an adjoining matron bedroom.

entries.description: McGonagall says she found the petrified Colin on the stairs beside grapes, apparently trying to visit Harry; Dumbledore had been heading downstairs for hot chocolate.
entries.model_notes: Reported find location and guessed destination; no floor, particular staircase or kitchen route established.

entries.description: Winter sunlight fills the ward in the morning, while high bed curtains conceal Colin’s bed from Harry’s view. Pomfrey brings breakfast on a tray.
entries.model_notes: Confirms curtains can block cross-ward sightlines, not merely screen changing.

entries.description: Ron and Hermione lock a cubicle to hide potion-making. An old cauldron sits on the toilet with a crackling waterproof magical fire underneath its rim. The keyhole permits Hermione to look out, and three pupils fit inside with difficulty.
entries.model_notes: Working cubicle lock/keyhole and cramped temporary lab; no dimensions or ventilation duct invented.

entries.description: The large dungeon holds twenty steaming cauldrons between wooden desks carrying brass scales and ingredient jars. Snape has his own desk at the front where pupils collect antidote.
entries.model_notes: Observed lesson layout and cauldron count; desk count remains unspecified.

entries.location: Potions dungeon to private stores — diversion
entries.description: Harry’s firework explodes Goyle’s Swelling Solution across the class. Hermione slips out during the confusion and returns with stolen ingredients beneath her robes; the firework’s blackened remains stay in the cauldron until Snape retrieves them.
entries.model_notes: The intended destination is Snape’s office, but actual intermediate route and unlocking are not witnessed.

entries.description: A noticeboard in the Entrance Hall holds the newly pinned Duelling Club announcement.
entries.model_notes: A fixed noticeboard location, without side of hall or mounting height.

entries.description: Dining tables vanish and a golden stage appears along one wall, illuminated by thousands of hovering candles beneath a velvety-black ceiling. Pupils gather standing, then pair up throughout the Hall; Harry and Malfoy’s demonstration uses its middle.
entries.temporal: Duelling Club, second week of December 1992
entries.model_notes: Large clear-floor use and wall-side stage. Lockhart reaches a wall when blasted backwards off the stage; no permanent platform assumed.

entries.description: Malfoy’s spell puts a long black snake on the floor. Lockhart sends it ten feet into the air before it lands and approaches Justin; Harry calms it with Parseltongue and Snape vanishes it in black smoke.
entries.model_notes: Dated mobile hazard; no permanent serpent enclosure or Hall access rule implied.

entries.location: Castle — blizzard daylight and Mandrake protection
entries.description: Snow visible from the tower dormitory becomes a blizzard by morning. Swirling grey snow at every window darkens the daytime castle. Herbology is cancelled so Sprout can fit socks and scarves to the Mandrakes.
entries.model_notes: Seasonal weather and plant care, not a closure of every classroom or greenhouse.

entries.description: Hufflepuffs sit at the back of the library between long lines of high shelves. Harry listens from concealment in the Invisibility section.
entries.model_notes: A subject shelving section, not a literal invisibility spell or separate hidden room.

entries.location: Hen-coop — rooster deaths and proposed ward
entries.description: Hagrid carries a dead rooster, says it is the second killed that term, and seeks permission to put a protective charm around the hen-coop.
entries.model_notes: The coop exists in Hagrid’s report but location is unstated. Fox or bugbear is his speculation, not confirmed fauna.

entries.location: Dark attack corridor — draught, classrooms and victims
entries.description: After passing Hagrid, Harry goes upstairs into a corridor where an icy draught through a loose windowpane has blown out the torches. Justin lies rigid halfway along, beside Nick floating black and smoky six inches above the floor. Spiders flee; classrooms on both sides are audible, with a door immediately beside Harry.
entries.model_notes: No floor number is supplied; keep distinct from the window-and-writing corridor unless identified later.

entries.description: Flitwick and Sinistra carry Justin up to the hospital wing; Ernie uses a conjured fan to waft the immobilised ghost Nick up the stairs.
entries.model_notes: Hospital wing is above the attack corridor. Ghost transport differs from carrying a solid patient.

entries.description: McGonagall takes Harry round a corner to a large ugly stone gargoyle. At Sherbet lemon it animates and hops aside; the wall behind splits, revealing a smoothly rising spiral stair like an escalator. The wall closes behind the riders as they circle upward to a gleaming oak door with a brass griffon knocker.
entries.model_notes: Explicit entrance mechanics, moving vertical circulation and materials; no entrance floor or compass side provided.

entries.location: Dumbledore’s office — circular room and furniture
entries.description: At the top of the stone stair a door opens silently into a large beautiful circular office. Silver instruments whirr and emit smoke on spindle-legged tables; portraits of sleeping former heads cover the walls. An enormous claw-footed desk has a high-backed chair behind it and the Sorting Hat rests on a shelf behind the desk.
entries.model_notes: Materials, plan and furniture relations explicit; instrument functions and room diameter unstated.

entries.location: Dumbledore’s office — phoenix perch and Burning Day
entries.description: A golden perch stands behind the door. Fawkes burns there into a smouldering ash pile on the floor, from which a chick emerges. Dumbledore says phoenixes normally have red-and-gold plumage, carry very heavy loads and heal through tears.
entries.model_notes: Observed office pet/perch event; carrying/healing claims are Dumbledore’s explanation and later usable transport constraints.

entries.location: Gryffindor dormitory — window curtains and owl access
entries.description: Hermione pulls back window curtains on a bright snowy Christmas morning, and Hedwig flies into the dormitory and lands on Harry’s bed.
entries.model_notes: Adds window curtains distinct from bed curtains. The owl’s precise entry opening is not stated.

entries.description: Twelve frost-covered Christmas trees decorate the Hall. Thick holly and mistletoe streamers cross the ceiling, which releases enchanted warm dry snow during dinner.
entries.model_notes: 1992 decoration differs from the previous Christmas; do not model the falling snow as wet indoor weather.

entries.location: Entrance Hall — banisters, armour and cleaning cupboard
entries.description: Cakes are set on the end of the banisters. Harry and Ron hide behind a suit of armour next to the front door, then move Crabbe and Goyle into a cupboard across the Hall among buckets and mops.
entries.model_notes: Specific entrance furnishings and cupboard relation. Banisters are not given an explicit height; cupboard is initially proposed as a broom cupboard.

entries.location: Myrtle’s bathroom — potion smoke, stone floor and cubicle limits
entries.description: Black smoke pours from the locked brewing cubicle, with three glasses on the toilet seat and a bubbling cauldron inside. The pupils choose separate cubicles because their transformed bodies would not fit together; Harry uses the middle one, with Ron to his right. The floor is cold stone.
entries.model_notes: Observed cramped space, fixtures and relative cubicle positions during Christmas brewing; do not infer total cubicle count from middle alone.

entries.description: Hermione says she took spare larger robes from the laundry for the transformations.
entries.model_notes: Establishes a laundry/storage function, without locating a laundry room or describing machinery.

entries.location: Myrtle’s bathroom to Slytherin dungeon passages
entries.description: Leaving the bathroom, Harry and Ron descend the marble staircase, then stone steps from the dungeon entrance. They wander deeper through deserted labyrinthine passages under the school for about fifteen minutes; Percy emerges from a side room before Malfoy leads them into the next passage.
entries.model_notes: Observed dungeon circulation and side room; elapsed time includes searching and does not set corridor lengths.

entries.description: Malfoy stops at bare damp stone wall. The password Pure-blood makes a concealed stone door slide open, allowing entry into Slytherin’s common room.
entries.model_notes: Password dated to Christmas 1992; no portrait, stair or visible handle is mentioned.

entries.description: A long low underground room has rough stone walls and ceiling, with round greenish lamps suspended on chains. A fire burns under an elaborately carved mantelpiece ahead of the entry; pupils use carved chairs by it and a pair of chairs farther back.
entries.model_notes: Explicit underground height impression and finishes. Lake windows or underwater position are not described in this passage.

entries.location: Chamber opening fifty years earlier — report
entries.description: Malfoy says the Chamber was opened fifty years earlier, before his father’s schooldays; a Muggle-born pupil died and someone was expelled. He says information about it was kept quiet.
entries.model_notes: Second-hand family story. Imprisonment is Malfoy’s guess, not confirmed.

entries.location: Slytherin common room escape to bathroom and hospital
entries.description: The boys run the length of the common room, pass out through the stone-wall entrance, go up the passage and steps to the dark Entrance Hall, then climb the marble staircase towards Myrtle’s bathroom. After finding Hermione transformed there, they propose taking her up to the hospital wing.
entries.model_notes: Observed return resolves no bathroom floor number. Hospital leg is proposed here and confirmed by later recovery scenes.

entries.location: Hospital wing — screened bed and bedside work
entries.description: Pomfrey puts curtains around Hermione’s bed to block passing pupils’ view during her weeks of recovery. A bedside table holds books brought by Harry and Ron.
entries.model_notes: Movable curtains are deployed for privacy; recovery lasts until early February.

entries.location: Hospital wing to writing corridor — upward route
entries.description: Leaving Hermione’s hospital dormitory, the boys climb stairs towards Gryffindor Tower. Filch’s voice comes from the floor above; going up and round a corner brings them to the earlier cat-attack site outside Myrtle’s bathroom.
entries.model_notes: Places this bathroom/attack corridor above the ward departure point in this scene, adding to unresolved floor constraints.

entries.description: Water seeps beneath the bathroom door and covers half the corridor. Inside, water has soaked walls and stone flooring and extinguished the candles; Myrtle’s wails echo. Her emergence from the toilet sends another wave across the floor, and a discarded diary lies under a sink.
entries.model_notes: Flooded extent and acoustic state; no drain capacity or quantified water depth.

entries.description: Riddle’s burnished gold special-services shield occupies a corner cabinet. His name also appears on an old Medal for Magical Merit and a list of former Head Boys.
entries.model_notes: Observed shield location and awards, separate from Ron’s earlier cleaning recollection.

entries.description: Pomfrey reports Mandrakes becoming moody and secretive, soon needing another repotting after their acne clears, before being ready to cut and stew for restoration.
entries.model_notes: Reported growth timetable, without a new greenhouse location or precise maturity date.

entries.location: Great Hall — Valentine decorations and roving dwarfs
entries.description: Large vivid pink flowers cover all the walls; heart-shaped confetti falls from a pale-blue ceiling. Twelve dwarfs wearing gold wings and carrying harps march in through the Entrance Hall doors and spend the day entering classes to deliver Valentines.
entries.model_notes: Dated decorative/event configuration, not permanent wall flowers.

entries.description: Harry retrieves a fresh ink bottle from a cabinet beside his four-poster.
entries.model_notes: Confirms personal bedside cabinet; no material or drawer count.

entries.description: The diary claims that in Riddle’s fifth year several pupils were attacked, a girl died, an accused pupil was expelled and a false accident story concealed the events. It offers a memory of the night he supposedly caught the culprit.
entries.temporal: Diary account of events fifty years earlier
entries.model_notes: Uncorroborated account presented by the diary; Hagrid’s guilt must not be treated as established.

entries.description: The June-thirteenth memory shows the same circular room and sleeping portraits, with Dippet at a candlelit desk, a curtained window looking onto a red sunset, and visitor seating. Fawkes and Dumbledore’s silver devices are absent.
entries.temporal: 13 June, fifty years before the 1992–93 investigation
entries.model_notes: Diary-mediated historical scene, not independently authenticated observation; no compass bearing inferred from sunset view.

entries.location: Headmaster’s office to Potions dungeon in diary memory
entries.description: Riddle leaves by the moving spiral stair past the gargoyle, walks to the Entrance Hall and sees young Dumbledore on the marble stairs, then descends the stone dungeon steps to the very classroom Harry knows as Snape’s Potions room. Its torches are unlit; a nearly closed door allows watching the passage.
entries.model_notes: Historical memory sequence, indicating apparent continuity of entrance mechanism and classroom use. No measured route or floor count.

entries.location: Dungeon creature cupboard in diary memory
entries.description: Following footsteps for perhaps five minutes beyond the Potions room and round a corner, Riddle confronts young Hagrid at a closed door beside a large box. The door is blasted open against an opposite wall and a large hairy many-legged creature escapes along the corridor.
entries.model_notes: Diary-mediated historical storage/escape scene. Room dimensions and creature destination are unstated; this is not the revealed Chamber of Secrets.

entries.description: In March several Mandrakes hold a noisy party in greenhouse three. Sprout says attempts to move into one another’s pots will signal full maturity.
entries.model_notes: Confirms continued greenhouse-three cultivation and reported maturity criterion.

entries.description: Harry’s trunk is emptied across the room, his cloak ripped on the floor, bedding stripped and a bedside-cabinet drawer pulled out with its contents over the mattress. The diary is missing.
entries.model_notes: Observed damage and drawer storage; the culprit’s house membership is the pupils’ deduction from the password, not verified access control.

entries.location: Great Hall to library and pitch
entries.description: At the marble staircase after breakfast Harry hears the voice again. Hermione runs upstairs towards the library while other pupils leave the Great Hall through the front doors for the pitch. Harry collects his broom in Gryffindor Tower before crossing the grounds to the changing room.
entries.model_notes: Upstairs library route, front-door stadium route; voice location/mechanism still unresolved.

entries.description: After the match is cancelled, McGonagall leads the boys back to the castle and up the marble staircase to the hospital wing.
entries.model_notes: Adds direct stadium-to-ward journey; hospital floor is not named.

entries.location: Hospital wing — adjacent beds and library attack report
entries.description: Hermione lies petrified in the bed next to Penelope Clearwater. McGonagall says they were found near the library with a small round mirror on the floor.
entries.model_notes: Ward arrangement observed; attack location and mirror discovery reported by the teacher.

entries.description: All pupils must return to common rooms by six, remain in dormitories thereafter, attend lessons under teacher escort and use bathrooms only with a teacher. Quidditch and evening activities are suspended; closure is threatened if the culprit is not caught.
entries.model_notes: Schoolwide time-dependent access restrictions, not newly built barriers.

entries.description: Teachers, Prefects and ghosts patrol the nighttime corridors in pairs. Under the Cloak the boys pass close to Snape on guard, then ease open the oak front doors and head towards Hagrid’s lit windows.
entries.model_notes: Observed implementation of emergency security; Cloak does not suppress sound and front doors can still be opened from inside.

entries.location: Hagrid’s cabin — defensive state and height clearance
entries.description: Hagrid answers the door with a crossbow. Inside, the kettle can spill onto the hearth, a teapot is smashed, the boys hide in a corner and Fang occupies a basket. When Hagrid stands abruptly his head grazes the ceiling.
entries.model_notes: Ceiling height is relative to Hagrid, not a numeric measurement; basket and hiding corner add furniture/usable space.

entries.description: Before being taken away, Hagrid tells unseen listeners that following the spiders would lead them to information, and asks for Fang to be fed.
entries.model_notes: A reported route clue rather than a mapped path; actual destination reviewed in the next chapter.

entries.location: Castle grounds — summer flowers and mullioned windows
entries.description: Sky and lake turn periwinkle blue and cabbage-sized flowers bloom in the greenhouses. Castle windows overlook Hagrid’s usual walking routes across the grounds; exterior sunlight falls on the walls and mullioned windows.
entries.model_notes: Adds explicit mullions and greenhouse flower scale; no window lattice pattern or individual room identified.

entries.description: Pomfrey bars visitors and speaks through a crack in the ward door, fearing further attacks on the patients.
entries.model_notes: Temporary security restriction; no newly fitted door lock described.

entries.location: Castle to Herbology — escorted route and compost heap
entries.description: Snape leads pupils from the Potions dungeon, out of the castle and across the vegetable patch to the greenhouses. They prune Abyssinian Shrivelfigs and carry cut stalks to a compost heap. Large spiders cross nearby earth towards the Forest.
entries.model_notes: Observed outdoor storage/waste feature and vegetation; spider heading is Harry’s interpretation.

entries.description: The common room remains crowded from six until after midnight because pupils have nowhere else to go. After two distant dormitory doors close, Harry and Ron leave under the Cloak.
entries.model_notes: Two audible dormitory closures, not a complete count or proof of their positions.

entries.description: The boys dodge patrols to the Entrance Hall, slide back the lock on the oak front doors and squeeze out quietly into moonlit grounds.
entries.model_notes: Explicit manually operable interior lock; no key, bar shape or exterior unlocking mechanism stated.

entries.location: Hagrid’s empty cabin — mantel and route to Forest
entries.description: They push open Hagrid’s door beneath dark windows, feed Fang fudge from a mantelpiece tin and leave the Cloak on the table. Fang leads to the Forest’s edge and a large sycamore.
entries.model_notes: Adds mantel storage and specific forest-edge tree; exact distance from cabin to sycamore unknown.

entries.location: Forest spider trail — canopy and off-path obstacles
entries.description: Following spiders for about twenty minutes along the path reaches trees dense enough to hide the stars. Spiders then leave the path; the boys follow slowly among roots and stumps, low branches and brambles for what seems at least another half-hour, noticing a downward slope.
entries.model_notes: Two timed segments include searching; do not convert to fixed distances. Downward slope is perceived, not surveyed.

entries.description: Breaking branches and rumbling to the boys’ right lead to a clearing within a circle of thick trees under a dense branch roof. The abandoned turquoise car lights the ground with its headlamps; surrounding thorns trap Fang.
entries.model_notes: Distinct preliminary clearing before the spider hollow. No surviving airborne function is demonstrated.

entries.description: Car-horse-sized spiders seize both boys and Fang and carry them deeper through trees to a vast hollow cleared of trees. Starlight reaches its leaf-covered floor; the carrying spider descends its steep rim.
entries.model_notes: Height above ground at capture is about ten feet in Ron’s sightline, not a universal spider height or hollow depth.

entries.location: Aragog’s hollow — central web and colony
entries.description: The large tree-cleared hollow is crowded with gigantic black hairy spiders. A misty domed web stands at its centre; blind grey-black Aragog, the size of a small elephant, emerges from it, while spiders surround the visitors.
entries.model_notes: Defines steep enclosed depression, open sky and central domed web, without metric diameter or spider count.

entries.location: Aragog — cupboard origin and Forest settlement
entries.description: Aragog says Hagrid raised him from an imported egg in a castle cupboard on table scraps. After blame for a girl’s death he escaped to the Forest, where Hagrid still visits and provided Mosag as a mate; the colony is their family.
entries.model_notes: Character history, consistent with but separate from the diary scene; cupboard has no floor or number here.

entries.location: Chamber monster — fear and historical bathroom death
entries.description: Aragog denies attacking humans, says the dead girl was found in a bathroom and identifies the real castle creature as ancient and feared above all others by spiders. He recalls sensing it moving through the school.
entries.model_notes: Reported sensory/historical evidence. Creature remains unnamed here; no pipe route yet established.

entries.location: Aragog’s hollow — car rescue and Forest exit
entries.description: The car drives down the steep hollow slope, loads the boys and Fang, climbs out and follows the widest tree gaps along a route it appears to know. Branches strike its windows; a large oak breaks a wing mirror. After roughly ten rough minutes the trees thin and the car stops at the Forest edge, then reverses back into the woods.
entries.model_notes: Ground vehicle can traverse this particular route; no paved track or numeric width implied. Ten minutes is this escape duration.

entries.location: Forest edge via cabin to Gryffindor Tower
entries.description: Fang runs from the exit through trees to Hagrid’s house. Harry retrieves the Cloak and finds Ron in the pumpkin patch; they return to the creaking front doors, cross the Entrance Hall, climb the marble staircase past patrolled corridors, enter the common room and ascend the winding dormitory stair.
entries.model_notes: Confirms patrols and return sequence. Common-room fire is reduced to glowing ash after the long excursion.

entries.description: Ron remembers Myrtle having been only three toilets away during their earlier bathroom work.
entries.model_notes: Character’s relative count, not necessarily three intervening toilets or a total cubicle count.

entries.description: Neville accidentally vanishes one leg of his desk; McGonagall restores it with a wand wave.
entries.model_notes: Transient furniture alteration; no permanent broken desk.

entries.description: Lockhart has been patrolling the fourth floor. While escorting pupils to History of Magic he leaves them with one corridor remaining; the boys peel into a side passage towards Myrtle’s bathroom but are diverted by McGonagall to visit the hospital wing.
entries.model_notes: Fourth floor is the patrol location, not a stated location of this lesson route. No precise adjacency inferred.

entries.location: Basilisk — inferred pipe route and reflected gaze
entries.description: A library page describes a huge long-lived basilisk with lethal eyes, venomous fangs, spider aversion and vulnerability to rooster calls. Hermione writes Pipes beneath it; Harry infers that the monster moves inside wall plumbing and that indirect views through camera, ghost, mirror or reflected water explain petrification instead of death.
entries.model_notes: Explicitly a deduction from book evidence, symptoms and sound, later to be checked against admissions and observed entrance. No pipe diameter can be deduced from every wall.

entries.description: The boys run downstairs from the ward into a deserted staff room. It is large and panelled, filled with dark wooden chairs, and contains an ugly wardrobe full of teachers’ cloaks on Harry’s left.
entries.model_notes: Adds lower staff-room relation and seating/wardrobe. Left is Harry’s viewpoint in the room, not a fixed compass wall.

entries.location: Staff room — overhead circulation and emergency announcement
entries.description: Hidden in the cloak wardrobe, the boys hear hundreds of people moving overhead as teachers enter. McGonagall’s amplified announcement has ordered pupils to dormitories and teachers to this room.
entries.model_notes: Acoustic relation to overhead circulation, no ceiling height or exact upper room identified.

entries.location: Writing corridor — second message and planned evacuation
entries.description: McGonagall reports a new message directly below the first, threatening that Ginny’s skeleton will remain in the Chamber. Teachers plan to send pupils home by Hogwarts Express the next morning.
entries.model_notes: Reported inscription and planned closure, not a witnessed skeleton or completed evacuation.

entries.description: After descending from Gryffindor Tower, the boys find Lockhart’s office largely stripped. Two open trunks hold robes and books; the wall photographs are boxed on the desk, a life-size self-poster is removed from behind the door, and a drawer is emptied. The office has an open window through which Ron throws the wand.
entries.model_notes: Adds window, drawer and door-back poster, with temporary packing clutter.

entries.description: They take Lockhart from his office down the nearest stairs, along the dark corridor with the shining messages, to Myrtle’s bathroom.
entries.model_notes: Explicit office-above-bathroom local route; retain alongside earlier conflicting second-floor office placement.

entries.description: Myrtle says she died in the end cubicle after unlocking its door to confront a boy speaking an odd language; she saw large yellow eyes vaguely near the sink in front of her toilet.
entries.temporal: Death fifty years earlier, recalled May 1993
entries.model_notes: Eyewitness ghost report, with deliberately vague source position; no exact historic sight ray or unchanged fixture claim.

entries.location: Chamber entrance — snake tap and sinking basin
entries.description: A sink in front of Myrtle’s toilet has pipes beneath and a tiny snake engraved on one copper tap, which Myrtle says never worked. English does nothing; a Parseltongue opening command makes the tap glow white and spin, then the sink sinks out of sight to expose a pipe wide enough for a man to slide into.
entries.model_notes: Observed language-triggered transformation. Reported faulty tap is distinct from the demonstrated mechanism; no complete sink plumbing schematic.

entries.description: The main pipe is dark, slimy, twisting and steeply descending, with smaller pipes branching in all directions. It finally levels and ejects the riders onto a damp stone tunnel floor where they can stand.
entries.model_notes: Narration places descent below the dungeons; Harry’s miles-down and Ron’s under-lake claims are guesses, not surveyed depths or coordinates.

entries.location: Chamber approach tunnel — wet floor and bones
entries.description: The dark stone tunnel has wet slimy walls, a damp floor that echoes/slaps underfoot and a bend beyond scattered small-animal bones, including a rat skull.
entries.model_notes: No fabricated drainage, lighting fixtures or tunnel dimensions. Wandlight limits the view.

entries.description: A huge vivid-green empty snakeskin lies curled across the tunnel floor. Harry estimates its former occupant at least twenty feet long.
entries.model_notes: Narrated size estimate for the snake based on skin, not a measured tunnel width or length.

entries.description: Ron’s broken wand explodes, dropping large chunks of ceiling into a solid rock barrier between Harry and Ron/Lockhart. Huge cracks remain above; Ron begins shifting the fallen stones while Harry continues beyond the skin.
entries.model_notes: Permanent-looking damage at this time; later clearance must be tracked separately. Passage not safely demolished by assumption.

entries.description: Beyond repeated tunnel turns stands a solid wall carved with two intertwined stone serpents whose eyes are large glinting emeralds. At Harry’s hissed Open, the wall cracks and its serpent-bearing halves slide out of sight.
entries.model_notes: Two distinct entry mechanisms: this door is beyond the bathroom pipe and rockfall. No inferred hinges or animated physical snakes.

entries.location: Chamber of Secrets — pillars, vault and lighting
entries.description: A very long dim chamber has towering stone pillars entwined with carved serpents, supporting a ceiling initially lost in darkness and later identified as vaulted. Greenish gloom casts long shadows; footsteps and laughter echo strongly. Stone snake carvings have hollow eye sockets.
entries.model_notes: Length and ceiling height remain unmeasured; apparent watching/moving carvings are Harry’s impressions, not verified animation.

entries.location: Chamber of Secrets — Slytherin statue and floor
entries.description: At the far end beyond the last pair of pillars, a statue as tall as the Chamber stands against the back wall. Its aged monkey-like face has a long thin beard descending almost to its sweeping stone robes; enormous grey feet rest on a smooth stone floor. Ginny lies between the feet and the diary near its toes.
entries.model_notes: Monument establishes chamber axis and end wall; no unsupported pool, central dais, bridge or stair.

entries.description: Riddle says he controlled Ginny through the diary, made her open the Chamber, strangle roosters, paint threatening wall messages and direct the serpent at victims. He says she stole the diary back from Harry’s deserted dormitory and wrote her farewell before coming below.
entries.model_notes: Character admission explains temporary incidents and paint material; retrospective details remain reported rather than independently witnessed.

entries.location: Chamber history — discovery and hostile Hagrid allegations
entries.description: Riddle says he spent five years learning the Chamber’s secrets and finding its entrance, then framed Hagrid and avoided reopening it under Dumbledore’s watch. He alleges Hagrid raised werewolf cubs beneath his bed and went into the Forest to wrestle trolls.
entries.model_notes: Hostile retrospective report; alleged cubs and trolls must not become confirmed permanent residents or a mapped enclosure.

entries.description: Phoenix song grows through the chamber, then flames erupt atop the nearest pillar and Fawkes appears there. He flies to Harry carrying the Sorting Hat and lands on his shoulder.
entries.model_notes: Observed arrival at a pillar, without a demonstrated continuous route from the office or a physical ceiling opening.

entries.description: Riddle addresses Slytherin in Parseltongue from between the pillars. The gigantic stone face moves and its mouth opens into a huge black hole; the basilisk slithers up from inside, drops to the stone floor and moves into the chamber.
entries.model_notes: Statue conceals a creature route. Its interior depth, storage cavity and connection to other pipes remain unspecified.

entries.location: Chamber — basilisk scale and combat clearance
entries.description: The bright-green serpent is as thick as an oak trunk, lifts its blunt head high between pillars and has sabre-like fangs. It thrashes against pillars, sweeps the floor with its tail and lunges into a chamber wall. Fawkes punctures its yellow eyes, allowing Harry to look directly at it.
entries.model_notes: Observed relative scale and collision clearance, not a measured body length; no pillar breakage or wall collapse stated.

entries.location: Chamber — summoned sword, corpse, blood and ink
entries.description: A silver sword with egg-sized rubies in its handle appears in the Sorting Hat. Harry kills the basilisk with it; the corpse and broken fang remain on the floor amid blood. Piercing the diary with the fang releases ink over the floor and destroys Riddle’s projection.
entries.model_notes: Temporary aftermath and magical object arrival; the blood/ink state must be dated, not made normal chamber material.

entries.location: Chamber inner doors — automatic closure and return rock gap
entries.description: The survivors step over the dead snake and leave through the stone doors, which hiss shut behind them. Returning up the turning tunnel, they find a sizeable hand-cleared gap in the rockfall, just large enough for Ginny, Fawkes and Harry to pass.
entries.model_notes: Updates rockfall from solid blockage to passable gap; not complete clearance or restored ceiling stability.

entries.description: Fawkes leads the return with softly gold-glowing wings through the dark tunnel to the pipe mouth, where Lockhart waits. Harry looks up the long dark shaft and sees no practical unaided climb.
entries.model_notes: Observed tunnel endpoint and lighting; inability to climb is implicit concern, not a detailed pipe cross-section.

entries.location: Phoenix lift through pipe — bathroom reset
entries.description: Holding Fawkes’s tail and one another, Harry, Ron, Ginny and Lockhart become light and fly up through the pipe. They land on Myrtle’s wet floor and the concealing sink slides back into place.
entries.model_notes: Demonstrated four-person lift and reset of the entrance. Return does not require a second spoken command in this account.

entries.description: The group exits into a dark deserted corridor, follows Fawkes’s glow and moments later reaches McGonagall’s office; Harry knocks and opens the door.
entries.model_notes: Short narrated transition without stairs or floor number. Do not silently resolve earlier floor conflicts by adding stairs.

entries.location: McGonagall’s office — hearth, desk and drawers
entries.description: The office has a fire with mantelpiece, chairs beside it, and McGonagall’s desk with drawers holding quill and ink. Harry lays the recovered Hat, sword and diary on the desk.
entries.model_notes: Office identity explicitly confirmed; no room shape or first-floor statement repeated here.

entries.location: McGonagall’s office — routes to ward and feast
entries.description: Dumbledore sends Ginny and later Lockhart up to the hospital wing, and tells Harry to go down to the feast.
entries.model_notes: Adds office-between-ward-and-feast vertical relations; no full route or direct adjacency.

entries.description: Leaving the office, Harry hears Dobby round a corner and runs along a dark corridor to the top of stairs. Dobby’s defensive magic throws Malfoy down the stairs onto a lower landing; a nearby window admits moonlight.
entries.model_notes: Confirms a corridor corner, stair flight and lower landing near office. Dobby later vanishes with a crack; no physical exit route needed for that departure.

entries.location: Great Hall — recovery feast and restored school state
entries.description: An all-night feast is attended in pyjamas after the petrified victims recover; Hagrid returns at half past three. Exams are cancelled and normal summer school life resumes, except for cancelled Defence classes.
entries.model_notes: Closes emergency occupancy/access state; normal school life does not explicitly repair the underground rockfall or remove the basilisk corpse.

entries.description: Ginny reports finding Percy and Penelope kissing in an otherwise empty classroom during their secret meetings around the school.
entries.model_notes: Reported unnamed classroom use; no floor, furnishings or identity with prior meeting rooms.

entries.location: School departure — Hogwarts Express and London gateway
entries.description: The pupils return by Hogwarts Express to King’s Cross, then join the crowd at the enchanted barrier and pass back into the Muggle station.
entries.model_notes: School-to-station transfer mode is omitted this year; do not reuse book 1’s boat detail as a fresh observation.

Complete chapter read, including the dream. Dobby’s warning describes no specific Hogwarts space or physical boundary; off-site confinement excluded.
Complete chapter read. Burrow, rescue flight and generic comments about house-elves in castles supply no new Hogwarts or nearby-boundary description.
Complete chapter read. London shops, Floo route and Burrow excluded from castle-boundary model; Hagrid’s school-cabbage report retained.
Complete chapter read. Imagined triumphant landing excluded as imagined; actual overflight order, external Hall sightline, dungeon office and retained dormitory recorded.
Complete chapter read; greenhouse numbering, layout, hazardous plants and classroom damage retained. No greenhouse material or fixed classroom floor invented.
Complete chapter read. Kept Hagrid’s rear patch distinct from the main vegetable patch. Advice about kelpies in a well does not locate a well at Hogwarts.

Complete chapter read. Recorded first-floor Myrtle report and explicit second-floor attack route separately; no silent floor reconciliation. Vanishing cabinet identity and overhead cause labelled as reports.

Complete chapter read. Recorded office-floor conflict and toilet adjacency explicitly. Founders’ account, chamber legend and unsuccessful searches remain reported history rather than observed geometry.
Complete chapter read. Dobby’s disappearance observed without naming its mechanism; Colin’s staircase location remains a teacher report and intended visit an inference.
Complete chapter read. Dumbledore’s moving staircase has no narrated floor number. The attack corridor’s classroom adjacency and hospital ascent kept distinct from the earlier attack location.
Complete chapter read. Detailed Slytherin route and room recorded without importing lake windows. Malfoy Manor’s unrelated secret chamber excluded.
Complete chapter read, including all diary dialogue and memory. Historical scenes labelled diary-mediated reports; no claim that the presented accusation proves who opened the Chamber.
Complete chapter read. Password-based assumptions about the theft not treated as proof; emergency rules distinguished from observed patrols and unlocked outward doors.
Complete chapter read. Distinct car clearing and spider hollow preserved; route durations remain unmeasured. Aragog’s claims distinguished from the actual rescue terrain.
Complete chapter read. Gaze/plumbing explanation first labelled inference; pipe depth and under-lake position remain unmeasured. Distinct sink entrance and emerald-serpent inner door catalogued.

Complete chapter read. Statue-mouth exit, true vault, combat clearances and return reset retained; no film-derived pool or bridge. Riddle’s claims remain admissions, with hostile fauna allegations unverified.
Complete chapter read. Recovery, office vertical relations and departure included. No unread paragraphs remain in book 2.
